what: One mutant per half of what this branch adds, not one for the change as a whole. A check that only reddens when everything is reverted proves one half is covered and says nothing about the other.
whatTheHalvesAre: the window is real — post-combat windows exist, contain refused steps, and the cohort in them is the group that was in the fight
the way round is real — it is searched for with bodies treated as walls, so a 'detour' is a different route and not the blind one re-derived
the discrimination is real — a creature standing on its own destination is one no yield may move, which is what makes the reach of a yield smaller than the reach of a way round

howToReproduce.runner: .artifacts/mutate-186.py — applies each replacement to one file, runs the checks, records the result and puts the file back in a finally block. The last run is the shipped tree, so the output ends with the state the branch carries.
howToReproduce.baseline: 4 of 4 green on the shipped tree, run last, after every mutation was put back.

mutants.name: S1a-refused-step-goes-unrecorded
mutants.half: the window is real: a refused step is what the measurement reads
mutants.edit: Move stops calling RecordMovementBlocked when the next tile carries a body; the step is still refused and the world behaves the same, only the canonical log stops saying so
mutants.reading: The sample collapses from 782 refused steps to 100 and the reach of a yield from 327 to 68, so 100 > 136 is false. The two checks that survive do so honestly: 100 refused steps is still above the floor of the sample check, and their detour share is still over a half. The one that catches it is the one that compares two reaches, because it is the only one that reads a ratio of two counts rather than one count.

mutants.name: S1b-move-ignores-bodies
mutants.half: the window is real: a step is refused because a body stands on the tile
mutants.edit: Move drops the occupancy refusal entirely
mutants.reading: Red, and by throwing rather than by counting: without the refusal two creatures share a tile and PlanTrafficActions, which builds a dictionary keyed by position, fails on the duplicate — `An item with the same key has already been added. Key: GridPoint { X = 5, Y = 7 }`. Reported as it happened. This mutant breaks the no-overlap invariant of 4.1 rather than the measurement, which is why S1a exists beside it.

mutants.name: S2-approach-rule-reverted
mutants.half: the checks are about the jam, not about the approach rule of #129
mutants.edit: ActCombatant goes back to `var destination = target.Position;` — the mutant of evidence/129-mutations.json
mutants.result: GREEN — and this is the intended result, reported rather than papered over
mutants.reading: The checks state what the mechanism is, and the mechanism is the same before and after #129: 372 refused steps instead of 782, detour share 0.930 instead of 0.931, a way round reaching 346 against a yield's 120. If this mutant reddened them, they would be checks about the approach rule, and the approach rule already has its own in PrototypeCombatApproachTests. The size of the clinch, which #129 does move, is measured in evidence/186-before-after-129.json and deliberately asserted nowhere: it is a corridor of six runs, and 13.4 says corridors are not requirements.

mutants.name: H1-cohort-read-after-resolve
mutants.half: the cohort is the fighters of the tick before the wave resolved
mutants.edit: the cohort is read from the snapshot of the tick the wave ended on instead of the one before it
mutants.reading: `Only 0 wave(s) over the matrix ended while the party was still alive`. ResolveWave has already turned every fighter into Waiting by the time that snapshot is taken, so the cohort is empty and there is nothing to measure. This is the one line of the harness on which the whole measurement stands.

mutants.name: H2-way-round-ignores-bodies
mutants.half: the way round is searched for with bodies treated as walls
mutants.edit: the second search drops its `bodies` argument, so it re-derives the route the simulation already walks
mutants.reading: `Only 0 of 782 ways round were strictly longer than the route the simulation walks with its eyes shut`. The detour share goes to a perfect 1.000 and means nothing at all, which is exactly the failure the first half of that check cannot see: it is a floor, and this mutant raises the number. The second assertion was added for this mutant and is the reason the 93.1 % can be believed.

mutants.name: H3-arrived-blocker-counts-as-yieldable
mutants.half: a creature standing on its own destination is one no yield may move
mutants.edit: the clause `blockerTarget == blocker.Position` becomes `blockerTarget == default`, so the 307 refused steps blocked by a creature that has arrived fall into the eligible class instead
mutants.reading: `A way round reached 728 refused steps after a fight and a yield could have cleared 617`. Drop the one clause of CanYield that says a working creature is not a creature you may shove, and the reach of a yield nearly doubles: this is the clause the whole discrimination between mechanism two and mechanism three rests on, and it is covered on its own.

whatIsNotCovered.what: The eligibility rule the harness applies is a rebuild of PrototypeWorld.CanYield from published state, not a call into it.
whatIsNotCovered.consequence: A mutant of CanYield itself leaves every count here unmoved. The two would only be pinned together by exporting CanYield, which would make the measurement unable to disagree with the code it measures — the same reason PrototypeCombatApproachTests restates the target rule instead of calling it.
whatIsNotCovered.howItIsBoundedInstead: The number is used only as an upper bound on what a yield could buy, and the conclusion of evidence/186-mechanism.json is one-sided: 728 against at most 327.
